title: Cost-Optimizer Watchdog — safe apply & rollback for batching/cache recommendations
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a watchdog and safe-apply pipeline that converts automated batching and KV-cache recommendations into guarded config changes. The watchdog should perform a dry-run, snapshot current runtime state, apply changes to a narrow canary cohort, monitor cost and correctness signals, and automatically reconcile or rollback to a known-good state when guardrail thresholds are breached. This ticket ties the cost-recommendation engine to a conservative execution path so finance-driven changes cannot cause silent correctness or latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Atomic apply operation: each automated change is associated with an op-id, a snapshot of prior config, and a persisted intent record
Dry-run and diff: the system runs a simulated apply and surfaces token-cost delta and estimated p95 latency change before scheduling a real apply
Canary rollout: changes are applied to <5% traffic or a small dedicated canary pool with configurable window
Automatic rollback: if any monitoring signal crosses configured guardrails during canary, the system must revert to the snapshot within SLA (target 30s for config switch)
State reconciliation: periodic reconciler ensures runtime matches desired state and retries/repairs partial failures idempotently
Audit trail: every automated apply/rollback generates an immutable event with links to PR, recommendation id, and metric snapshot
E2E test coverage for the happy path, canary failure path, and reconciliation after control-plane restart
progress_updates: 2026-02-27: RFC drafted for watchdog flow; circulated to PM and Reliability for initial feedback (link in design_docs)
2026-03-03: Spike completed: simulated applies + snapshot/restore prototype that toggles batching window; observed no correctness regressions in synthetic suite
2026-03-08: Engineering review with Runtime team; requested addition of op-id ordering to prevent out-of-order reconciles
2026-03-12: Canary harness skeleton merged (PR-#4219); added canary metric set (cost delta, p95 latency, error-rate, token-drop rate)
2026-03-14: Started integration tests on staging with real KV-cache toggles; discovered race when reconcile triggered mid-apply — mitigation planned in notes
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature gates behind 'watchdog' flag; 2) Run 24h synthetic dry-run on staging; 3) Enable canary on <5% traffic for 2h; 4) Gradually increase to 25% with manual check; 5) Auto-advance to global only when all guardrails stable for 24h
revert_strategy: Before any apply, persist a state snapshot and op-id. If a guardrail triggers, call immediate revert with the snapshot. If revert fails, mark the op as FAILED and escalate to on-call with runbook link. The reconciler will attempt auto-repair once for transient failures, then stop and require manual intervention.
test_plan: Unit tests for op-id ordering and idempotency, integration tests that flip batching/cache flags in staging, chaos tests that restart control-plane mid-apply, and load tests verifying p95 latency impact under recommend changes.
notes: Tradeoffs: aggressive batching reduces per-token cost but increases tail latency; guardrails must balance finance goals with SLAs
Reconciliation: use op-id and timestamp monotonicity to ensure stale desired-state writes don't overwrite newer runtime changes
Open questions: escalation thresholds for multi-customer dedicated pools, and how to surface recommendation confidence to SREs
Next steps: add idempotent operation API on runtime, finalize dry-run diff UI in console, and schedule security review for rollout automation (optional)
